cohort: The study included 228 children born in 226 deliveries at the Department for Gynaecology and Obstetrics of the Vukovar hospital between May 1st, 1991, and November 19th, 1991, during wartime conditions.
finding: Despite severe wartime conditions, including lack of antenatal care, no significant deviations were found in obstetric complications, early perinatal outcome, or overall perinatal mortality, possibly due to psychosomatic adaptation to war-related stress.
mod_finding: The study reported a 10.6% caesarean section rate, 65.4% episiotomy rate, and 1.32% vaginal deliveries in breech presentation.
followup_time: Perinatal period (up to 7 days post-birth for perinatal deaths, Apgar scores taken at birth)
